name: prov
comment: The Prism's provenance checker (app/src/PrismProv.lex.tex, the guest 'prov') held to W3C's Constraints of the PROV Data Model (PROV-CONSTRAINTS, Recommendation 30 April 2013), reading the PROV-N notation (Recommendation 30 April 2013). The request is 'check', a newline and a PROV-N document; the answer is 'valid', 'invalid' and the numbers of the constraints that do not hold, 'malformed' when the text is not a PROV-N document, or 'unjudged' when normalization would pass the guest's bounds (4,000 statements or 30,000 existential variables in one instance). 'tests' is every PROV-N case of the PROV working group's constraints test suite, as the 'suite' page lists them and as W3C serves them under 'base', each pinned by SHA-256 and kept at app/specs/standards/texts/<sha256>. A case's file name is W3C's verdict: PASS is a valid document, FAIL is not, and the c numbers are the constraints the case is about; DM marks a case that is not a document of the data model, which this reader refuses as malformed. 'answer' is the guest's answer: W3C gives the verdict, and the numbers in an 'invalid' answer are the checker's own reading, each one among the file name's c numbers except in type-f4-FAIL-c53, where Inference 15 gives the generation and the usage that share an identifier two influences with that identifier, so Constraint 23 fails beside 53. 'examples' carries the PASS cases byte for byte as the guest's acceptance vectors after the verb line, and app/specs/prov/invalid/spec.json carries the FAIL cases the same way for the guest 'prov-invalid' (the same module: one guest build carries at most about 110 vectors); cases W3C serves under two names with the same bytes are one vector; nothing else is an acceptance vector. 'shown' names, for each numbered inference or constraint, the cases whose verdict changes when that one rule is switched off in the checker: those are the rules this suite shows enforced. The suite cannot show the others (its ordering cases outside 42 and 45 are all PASS cases, and no case turns on Inferences 5 to 18, 20 and 21 or Constraints 22, 50, 51 and 53 alone), so they stay in ST-01's debt, and a document with a repeated bundle identifier (section 7.2, answered 'invalid 7.2') has no case at all.
